title: Orange and apricot compote with yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oranges, dried apricots, honey, Greek yoghurt, almonds and cinnamon are all plain larder and fridge foods.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item on Tesco shelves at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one small pan and a sharp knife, and cutting away orange peel and pith is within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: Four oranges, 150g apricots, 500g yoghurt and 50g almonds make a sensible breakfast for four, and a 10-minute simmer in 200ml water will plump the apricots into a light syrup.

honest_times.reason: Toasting the almonds, halving the apricots, zesting, and peeling and slicing four oranges fit believably in 12 minutes, and the 10-minute simmer matches the cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon appear in the steps, nothing unlisted is used beyond water, and flaked almonds are the same food as the almonds id.

seasonal_feel.reason: Oranges are at their best in early March and they make up the bulk of this warm compote, which suits a chilly morning.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no fancy or preachy language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit with a generous serving of Greek yoghurt and toasted almonds gives a filling breakfast with protein, and only a modest tablespoon of honey.
